findings.observed: The second put raises OverflowError only after appending; len(q) is 2 and subsequent gets return both 'kept' and 'rejected'.
findings.expected: OverflowError is raised without changing the queue; len(q) remains 1 and only 'kept' can be retrieved.
findings.explanation: TaskQueue.put mutates _items before checking capacity, violating the failed-put atomicity guarantee. Check fullness before appending (or undo the append before raising).

findings.trigger: a = TaskQueue(2); b = TaskQueue(2); a.put(None); len(b); b.get()
findings.observed: len(b) becomes 1 and b.get() returns None even though no item was put into b.
findings.expected: b remains empty (len(b) == 0) and b.get() raises IndexError.
findings.explanation: The mutable default items=[] is shared by every constructor call that omits items, so nominally separate queues share storage. Use a fresh list per instance, such as a None default followed by allocation in __init__.
